recipes.name: Spicy Baked Feta (Feta Psiti)
ingredients_raw: 2 tablespoons crushed red pepper flakes, or as needed

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Place the feta in an ovenproof baking dish. Drizzle with olive oil. Cover liberally with pepper flakes, and sprinkle with oregano.
Bake, uncovered, in the preheated oven until feta is soft, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Baked Feta (Feta Psiti)
raw_recipe.description: This is such an easy appetizer that never fails to impress! People are familiar with feta, but this traditional Greek way of preparing is not as well known. The salty/sour taste of the feta offsets the heat of the chili flakes - so don't be afraid to load them on!

video.description: When you need a quick appetizer that’s sure to impress, bring together salty, tangy fresh feta with plenty of red pepper and bake up a spread that will liven up the entire party! Cover a block or two of feta with olive oil, red pepper flakes and oregano, bake, and serve up this creamy and traditional appetizer with toasts, crusty bread or crackers.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is simple, yet AMAZING. I don't know what that other guy was talking about, there are no additional flavors needed. Maybe he had some cheap/bad feta or an unrefined palette. Anyway, I just can't say enough about how wonderful this recipe is. When I ate it with my husband and our three year old child, we all could not stop discussing how wonderful it was with our friends for the next week. Here's a little tip: follow the recipe exactly, add nothing. It is PERFECT.

There were two recipes, this one and a sweet one for baked feta. I decided to split my block of Vigo Feta into two and make a sweet and spicy appetizer. Other than that I changed nothing in either recipe. Couldn't be easier and it was a huge hit on the charcutier board. So, the left side was the red pepper and oregano; the right was honey and thyme. I liked both by themselves but I think the winner for me was mixing the two on the bread.

We've made this delicious feta recipe numerous times and more recently on the BBQ (on aluminum foil with the sides crimped up to catch drips). We discovered that we needed lots of chili pepper flakes when using the "stale" stuff from the Bulk Barn. Just the other day with friends, I crushed up some dried chilis I stored in a jar from last year's garden, and boy oh boy, what an amazing flavour! We BBQ'd 2 large 1/4 inch slabs and ate them with garlic buttered toasted pitas and everyone including kids was ranting and raving over the flavour. So simple and so good.

I am giving this 4 stars as written because it is bland as is. I had to doctor it up, then it became 4.5 stars. I didn't use sliced feta, instead I used crushed feta (I thought it would 'melt' more and it did) and I added some garlic and tomato sauce. I served with warm pita chips.

Great appetizer! So easy to make and tastes great. The heat is offset well by the cheese. I eyeballed the measurements, but followed the ingredients. Also, I used a mortar and pestle to crush the spices for fresher flavor. Will definitely make again.

Excellent idea. I drizzled with garlic infused olive oil and added cherry tomatoes and juice from 1/2 a lemon. Huge hit at my cocktail party last night. Be sure to enjoy when it's hot, as the feta hardens back up as it cools.

Seems like roasting softens the tang. Definitely add minced garlic, garlic powder, paprika, rosemary & oregano with other ingredients for a more diverse & beautiful offering. Gone in 1 bite. Okay, maybe 2...no crackers needed. They didn't last that long.
I added a 3 tablespoons of plain Greek yogurt to keep it smooth. A hit with everyone.

Excellent flavor, although on other tries I did add a bit of garlic and/or garlic powder which intensified the flavors. DO NOT make the mistake of using fat free feta; once I made it with the fat free as that was all the store had, but it failed miserably as the feta does not melt/soften. Simple and excellent recipe with few ingredients.

This was a super easy appetizer and a definite hit. I was worried about all the pepper flakes but they added the PERFECT contrast to the sour-salty of the cheese. I served this with crusty bread and it was a big hit! Wouldn't change a thing. One note though, I did have to cook it for almost twice the amount of time to get the cheese to be hot all the way through.
I will make again, but it was way too much red pepper for us. Will probably use 1/2 recommended quantity
Beyond easy and so delicious
This was the best surprise! Only added a sprinkle of garlic powder and followed the recipe. It has endless possibilities for making in the future. Served with wheat thins and it was gobbled up!
WOW will be making this again - no changes needed for me
Was delicious and easy. (Greek food is fantastic- I am proud to be Greek :) )
Took it to a party and everybody loved it.
This was wonderful and so easy to prepare. Served it with pita chips and everyone loved it. It's nice to have simple recipes like this on hand for happy hour gatherings. Thanks for sharing!

I made this exactly as the recipe said and was dissapointed. WAY to salty! I am thinking that instead of the spices used, it would be better using garlic or something else. Will not make again the way it is.

Delicious, simple, quick and inexpensive = a perfect party appetizer. I served it with plain sliced french bread but will do crackers next time for texture. Cover the cheese LIBERALLY with herbs and red pepper flakes - the feta perfectly balances them.
So interesting and delicious!! Very surprised that it wasn't too spicy...it's perfect for people who enjoy a little heat!
